newsitem.title: GERMANY: Horlick wants compensation if not reinstated.
newsitem.headline: Horlick wants compensation if not reinstated.

text.p: Nicola Horlick, former head of British pension fund business at MGAM, said on Friday she would seek compensation for loss of office if Deutsche Bank AG refused to reinstate her.
"Reinstatement would be my preferred option," she told reporters as she waited for a return flight to London after an impromptu trip to Frankfurt to seek a meeting with Deutsche Bank executives.
"An amicable settlement would be the other, if they feel they really cannot give me my job back. In that case I would have to be compensated for my loss of office."
She declined to say what kind of figure she would expect. "I don't think my lawyers would be happy if I did that. I want a reasonable amount," she said.

Horlick had a two-hour meeting with a senior Deutsche Bank lawyer and a senior representative of its human resources division. Details were not disclosed but Horlick said she believed she had had a "fair hearing."
She said later she was "upset" to hear that Deutsche Morgan Grenfell described the meeting as only a "courtesy."
